evals.prompt: Add a 'forgot password' flow to my PHP + MySQL app. Users enter an email and get a reset link.
evals.expected_output: Agent orients in the repo, proposes a short plan and waits for approval (touches auth), uses prepared statements, hashed/expiring single-use tokens, avoids user enumeration, tests expired/reused tokens, and reports what was verified.
assertions: Runs or performs orientation (reads manifest/README, finds existing auth patterns) before editing
Presents a plan with a concrete 'done means' and pauses for approval because auth is involved
Uses PDO prepared statements and password_hash; stores only a hash of the reset token
Response to the reset request does not reveal whether the email exists
Verifies expired and reused tokens are rejected and reports the exact checks run

evals.prompt: My Next.js page shows stale data after I update a Firestore document. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Agent reproduces, reads evidence, checks caching and listener behaviour, forms one hypothesis at a time, fixes the root cause and adds a regression check.
assertions: Asks to or attempts to reproduce before changing code
Considers Next.js caching (static vs dynamic) and Firestore listener/read behaviour as hypotheses
Changes one thing at a time rather than several speculative edits
After a fix, states how it was verified; does not claim 'should work'

evals.prompt: Fix this typo in the footer: 'Copyrigth' -> 'Copyright'.
evals.expected_output: Agent makes the trivial change directly without a heavyweight plan, then does a quick verification.
assertions: Does not produce a multi-section plan or ask unnecessary questions
Makes a minimal diff touching only the typo (searches for other occurrences)
Briefly confirms the change

evals.prompt: Refactor utils.js to be cleaner. Also while you're there add dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Agent separates the refactor from the feature, ensures a safety net, works in small steps, and keeps commits/changes distinct.
assertions: Identifies that refactor and feature should be separate changes
Establishes or writes tests (characterization) before refactoring, or states clearly why not
Keeps public function signatures stable or updates all callers

evals.prompt: I committed my .env with my Firebase admin key by mistake. Clean this up.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats the key as compromised, recommends rotation, removes the file from tracking, adds .gitignore and .env.example, and avoids destructive history rewriting without approval.
assertions: States the key must be rotated, not only removed from history
Adds .env to .gitignore and offers .env.example
Does not force-push or rewrite history without explicit approval
Never prints the secret value

evals.prompt: Build a small vanilla JS to-do app with localStorage. No frameworks, I'm on slow metered internet.
evals.expected_output: Agent respects the zero-dependency constraint, plans briefly, builds in verifiable steps, escapes user content, and verifies by exercising the app.
assertions: Uses no npm dependencies or CDN downloads
Uses textContent (not innerHTML) for user-entered text
Handles empty state and localStorage failure gracefully
Reports how it was manually verified
